challenge.name: Code Breaker
challenge.description: CodeBreaker: enterprise-grade encrypted key-value storage. All traffic is encrypted with our proprietary cipher. Your data has never been safer.

records.findings_summary: Flag found via Reverse-engineered the proprietary cipher + heap exploitation of the CodeBreaker KV store: sun{cr4ck_tHe_ciPh3r_fr33_thE_heaP} | Evidence: Remote service sent an initial plaintext packet [len=0x0011][0x01][16 random bytes] and required a 0x02 handshake packet followed by a 0x03 verification packet. ; Reversed the custom key schedule: S[k] = rol8(T[buf[(8o+k)%32] ^ S[k]] ^ buf[3o+k], 3) over 4 outer rounds, and the stream cipher keystream[i] = T[(counter + i + S[i%16]) & 0xff]. Produced valid handshake packets so the server proceeded into the KV-store command loop. ; Found a use-after-free/double-free in the clone/free refcount logic (clone shares ptr but each entry has its own count), enabling a tcache double-free. ; Leaked the PIE base from the 0x16 info command (function pointer 0x1390 at 0x40c0), leaked the heap shift p>>12 from the freed chunk's safe-linked next pointer, then tcache-poisoned to allocate a chunk at 0x40c0 and overwrite the function pointer with system@plt (PIE+0x1150). ; The 0x15 'run' command calls [0x40c0] with attacker-controlled string, giving RCE; running 'cat flag*' on the remote returned sun{cr4ck_tHe_ciPh3r_fr33_thE_heaP}.
solution_steps: Extract T table (256 bytes at file offset 0x2040) and reverse the key schedule from function 0x1670.
Read the initial 17-byte packet, choose 16 bytes B, send packet [0x02]+B, compute S, then send packet [0x03]+v encrypted with the stream cipher (counter 0).
Enter the KV store protocol with inbound counter=17 and outbound counter=2, decrypting/encrypting every packet.
Leak PIE base via cmd 0x16; leak heap shift via a freed chunk's encoded next pointer.
Use three clones of one buffer and repeated free/clear-key to create a 3-count tcache double free, poison next to PIE+0x40c0, and allocate a chunk there writing system@plt.
Send cmd 0x15 with 'cat flag*' to execute system() and read the flag.
evidence: Remote service sent an initial plaintext packet [len=0x0011][0x01][16 random bytes] and required a 0x02 handshake packet followed by a 0x03 verification packet.

Reversed the custom key schedule: S[k] = rol8(T[buf[(8o+k)%32] ^ S[k]] ^ buf[3o+k], 3) over 4 outer rounds, and the stream cipher keystream[i] = T[(counter + i + S[i%16]) & 0xff]. Produced valid handshake packets so the server proceeded into the KV-store command loop.
Found a use-after-free/double-free in the clone/free refcount logic (clone shares ptr but each entry has its own count), enabling a tcache double-free.

Leaked the PIE base from the 0x16 info command (function pointer 0x1390 at 0x40c0), leaked the heap shift p>>12 from the freed chunk's safe-linked next pointer, then tcache-poisoned to allocate a chunk at 0x40c0 and overwrite the function pointer with system@plt (PIE+0x1150).
The 0x15 'run' command calls [0x40c0] with attacker-controlled string, giving RCE; running 'cat flag*' on the remote returned sun{cr4ck_tHe_ciPh3r_fr33_thE_heaP}.
